example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading and Harbor Office Supply, account NB-2210, statement dated 25 September. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.harbor-statement-25-september.pdf: the name of the statement file that Harbor sent
chosen.Vendor_Statement_Recon_HarborOfficeSuppl: the file name that the skill gives the workpaper, with the statement date in the example year 2026

messages.text: Harbor Office Supply sent us a statement. Can you check it against our books?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
Please attach Harbor's statement, as a PDF or CSV. I always need it, because MosoFin cannot read it.
Which company is the statement addressed to, and what account reference does it show?
What is your cutoff date? What date is on the statement?
Does the statement list every open item, only overdue items, or a balance brought forward?
Do you keep a dispute log? Are you holding back any invoices on purpose?
Which suppliers do you reconcile, how often, and who owns the exceptions?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. Statement attached. It's addressed to Northbrook Trading, account NB-2210. Our books are at 30 September, the statement is dated 25 September. It lists every open item. No disputes. We do Harbor monthly, and AP owns the exceptions.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I reconcile **Harbor Office Supply**'s open-item statement to **Northbrook Trading**'s supplier ledger, account reference **NB-2210**. I read the ledger and payments through MosoFin.
messages.after: Your cutoff is **30 September** and the statement is dated **25 September**. So I reconcile at 25 September, and I list each ledger item from 26 to 30 September on its own. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
messages.summary: 7 reads in one batch, past your cutoff. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: I matched Harbor's lines to your ledger, document number first. INV-0042 on the statement is document 42 in your books. Then I took your ledger back to the statement date:

card.title: Your ledger at the statement date

messages.after: Both items are timing. Harbor shows them on its next statement.

messages.text: Harbor's statement says **$20,710.00**. Two of its lines are not in your books:

card.title: Your ledger to Harbor's statement, 25 Sep
rows: + INV-0049, 18 Sep, not in your books
− Credit note CN-0011, 12 Sep, not in your books

messages.after: INV-0049 matches nothing in your books at any tier. It is not under a second Harbor record or in a sibling company. So it is a **possible bill you never recorded**. Please ask Harbor for a copy.

messages.text: Harbor also owes **you** money. CN-0011 is a credit for returned chairs. It relates to INV-0031, which you paid in full on 5 September.
messages.after: You have no open Harbor bill, so the credit has nothing to go against. Ask Harbor for a refund, or take it off the next bill. Did you receive the INV-0049 goods and return those chairs?

messages.text: Yes. We got the goods, and we returned the chairs. Both are real.
Thank you. I propose one entry now:

card.title: Proposed entry, not posted
head: Entry
Amount
Evidence
rows: Accrual at 30 Sep: debit expense or inventory, credit accrued liabilities
INV-0049 on Harbor's statement, and your yes

messages.after: The accrual reverses on 1 October. When the invoice copy arrives, the invoice takes its place. A statement line does not support a credit entry, so please ask Harbor for the CN-0011 document too. A person posts entries and contacts Harbor. I do neither.

messages.text: Your workpaper has six sheets: the summary, the matched items with their tier, the exceptions, the proposed entry, the supplier ranking and the coverage. AP owns both exceptions. Please give each one a target date.
messages.after: Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file?
Do you want me to save your settings for next month?

messages.text: Done. I saved Harbor's account reference, its statement style, your monthly programme and the two open exceptions with their owner. Next month, the run starts from them.
